headline_answer: YES. The premise that no >15-inch e-paper frame has ever reached a real owner is FALSE, and it is false twice over. (1) Retail: PocketBook's InkPoster Tela 28.5in ($2,399) and Affresco 31.5in ($1,699) have been on general sale in the US since roughly Nov-Dec 2025, are 'Add to cart' in stock today, and an independent reviewer (Fstoppers, 21 Dec 2025) physically received and photographed one. (2) Crowdfunded: Fraimic's Large Canvas (31.5in Spectra 6) began shipping to Kickstarter backers in the last week of July 2026, and named backers posted receipt confirmations on the campaign's public comment wall on 4-5 Aug 2026 ('the Large frame came today', 'I am backer 1102 and I just received 1 large (31 inch) screen... works great'). So 'open but risky' does NOT collapse into 'does not exist'. What IS true is that the specific vendors the survey flagged as most open are the ones still not delivering at size: BLOOMIN8's 28.5in is ~10 months past its promised October 2025 date with zero backers reporting a unit, and InkJoy's 25.3in/28.5in are ~3 months late with production only targeted for mid-August 2026. Both those vendors HAVE delivered their small (7.3in-13.3in) SKUs, so the pattern is not 'vendor cannot ship', it is 'the large panel is the part that slips'. And the true horror story in this category is Galari (Kyoto): $339,557 from 737 backers in March 2025, promised September 2025, and as of August 2026 still has no supplier for the panel and is redesigning its PCB.

campaigns.name: Fraimic Large Canvas (31.5in)
campaigns.funded_date: 2025-10 (campaign ended October 2025; exact end date not confirmed from a source I fetched)
campaigns.promised_ship: May 2026 (stated as 'Estimated delivery' on every Large reward tier)
campaigns.current_status: SHIPPING AND ARRIVING. Update #15 (21 Jul 2026) 'Large Fraimic Units Have Arrived at the Port! Shipping Begins Soon'. Creator comment 6 days before my read: 'We've officially started shipping Large Fraimic units. Fulfillment is now underway'. Creator 2 days before my read: 'Large units only started shipping last week'. fraimic.com lists Large Canvas at $1,299 (MSRP $1,499), currently 'Sold out', 'Ships Early August', 9 customer reviews.
campaigns.delivery_evidence: DECISIVE, from non-vendor backers on the public Kickstarter comment wall, read 2026-08-05: (a) Jacob Crosetto, ~8 hours before read: 'I received my Standard frame back in June and the Large frame came today. No issues with set up and - while a little slower at displaying the images than expected - I continue to be beyond impressed.' (b) Dwoa/Lex Schut, backer #1102, 1 day before read: 'i just received 1 large (31 inch) screen, but i ordered a set of two... The screen i did receive works great!' Creator replied confirming the second unit had shipped. Reward tiers show roughly 690 pledges containing a Large unit (~900 Large units total). Independent press exists but only tested the 13.3in Standard: New Atlas (Joe Salas) tested a preproduction Standard; Notebookcheck (17 May 2026) tested a pre-release 13.3in sample. Forbes (21 Jul 2026, Mark Sparrow) states 'The Fraimic Smart Canvas is shipping now in two sizes from fraimic.com' but shows no evidence of hands-on testing. So the >15in delivery evidence is backer-reported, not press-reported, but it is multiple named backers with dates and specifics.

campaigns.name: InkJoy Frame 25.3in and 28.5in
campaigns.funded_date: 2026-01 (campaign ended January 2026; HK$3,232,767 from 676 backers, 8,313% funded - exact end date not confirmed from a source I fetched)

campaigns.name: Galari: The Ever-Changing Art Frame
campaigns.vendor: Galari (Kyoto, Japan; spun out of Kyoto Institute of Technology). Kickstarter profile: 'First created - 0 backed'
campaigns.funded_date: 2025-03-26 ($339,557 from 737 backers against a $19,056 goal; 'Project We Love')
campaigns.promised_ship: September 2025 on all reward tiers (backers repeatedly cite August 2025 from the campaign timeline)
campaigns.current_status: CATASTROPHIC. As of comments read 2026-08-05 - about 11 months past the promised date - there is still no product. A backer summarising the June 2026 update: 'we get an update you are still searching for a supplier for the panel, need to redesign the pcb'. The creator admitted the demo prototype was 'built using a Raspberry Pi and off-the-shelf Waveshare modules' and that custom PCBs still have to be designed and validated against the supplier's panel batch. Refund requests are being refused. The creator is still posting (roughly monthly) and still replying in comments.
campaigns.delivery_evidence: None. Single unnamed size, MSRP $699. Backer sentiment has turned: 'we all are scammed', 'I don't know if they're scammers or just absolutely dreaming hobbyists', 'Misleading a whole community will lead to lawsuit'. One backer has already bought a competitor product instead and reports it 'works magnificently'. Included here not because it is >15in (size unconfirmed, probably 13.3in) but because it is the single best-documented base-rate failure in this exact product category, from a well-reviewed, Project-We-Love, 1,700%-overfunded campaign.

historical_precedents.what_happened: VERIFIED IN SUBSTANCE, WRONG IN ONE DETAIL. The bricking story is real and corroborated by two independent sources. Memento sold a ~35-inch, 3:2, 4K digital art frame for approaching $900, funded via Kickstarter around 2016. The company went out of business in late 2018 / 2018-19. The frame was 100% cloud-dependent: 'The only way to get photos onto the frame is through the app via the cloud servers', and even the USB port required an active server connection, so when the servers went dark owners could not load images and could not even complete initial setup. Frames became, in the sources' words, 'an expensive paperweight'. A small community keeps a minority of units alive. THE CORRECTION: Memento was NOT an e-paper frame - it was a high-resolution emissive panel. Do not cite it as an e-paper precedent; cite it as the canonical cloud-dependency precedent, which is how the independent e-ink frame reviewer actually uses it.

sources.what_it_supports: Out of business late 2018; ~$900; 35in 4K 3:2; cloud-only image path including a USB port that needed the server; 'expensive paperweight'

Independent corroboration from an e-ink frame reviewer: 'Memento is a good example of what can go wrong: once its servers were shut down, the owners were left with expensive, essentially useless hardware' - and it is used explicitly as the reason to prefer cloud-free frames

historical_precedents.product: Electric Objects EO1 / EO2 digital art frame
historical_precedents.what_happened: A second, independent instance of the same failure mode, and the closest analogue to this buyer's use case (an internet-connected fine-art display). Electric Objects raised on Kickstarter in 2014, shipped EO1 and EO2, was acquired by GIPHY in 2017, and the hardware team was wound down. Years later owners report the EO2 can no longer be reconnected to Wi-Fi because the configuration app is gone from the App Store, so a device that is physically fine is unrecoverable. CAVEAT ON MY SOURCING: the owner report I fetched (comedian Adam Conover's Mastodon post) returned only the opening fragment 'My beloved Electric Objects EO2 digital art frame...' - I could not retrieve the full text or its date from that page, and the supporting detail about the app removal came from search-result summaries I did not independently open. Treat the specifics as medium-confidence; treat the pattern (art-frame company acquired, service and app abandoned, hardware stranded) as well-established.

sources.what_it_supports: An owner publicly complaining about an EO2 digital art frame; I could only extract the opening fragment of the post, so this supports 'an owner posted about it', not the full detail

historical_precedents.what_happened: The best-documented in-category crowdfunding failure to date, and it is CURRENT, not historical. Funded 26 March 2025 at 1,700% of goal ($339,557 / 737 backers / Project We Love badge), promised September 2025. Seventeen months after funding and eleven months past the promise, there is still no panel supplier and the PCB is being redesigned; the demonstrated prototype turns out to have been a Raspberry Pi driving off-the-shelf Waveshare modules. Refunds are being refused on the grounds that the money is committed. Note that the vendor is still communicating monthly - so 'vendor still posts updates' is NOT a safety signal.

sources.what_it_supports: Every element above, in the creator's and backers' own words, read 2026-08-05
Funding total, backer count, funding period, Project We Love badge, first-time creator

historical_precedents.what_happened: POSITIVE precedent. A small design-driven startup ran a Kickstarter in early 2025, overfunded, and moved to retail launch with a Spectra 6 e-ink frame. Its differentiator is architectural: images transfer over NFC/Bluetooth by tapping a phone to the frame's corner, with no cloud storage and no Wi-Fi requirement - explicitly designed so a Memento-style server shutdown cannot brick it. The reviewer did not state backer-delivery dates, so 'delivered to backers on time' is not established, only 'reached retail'. Size not stated in the review; other sources put the Reflection Frame at 13.3in, which I did not verify.

sources.what_it_supports: Kickstarter in early 2025, overfunded, retail launch, NFC/BLE local-only transfer with no cloud, and the explicit anti-Memento design rationale; also a note that competitor Nixplay moved to a subscription model

historical_precedents.what_happened: POSITIVE precedent for the 'tiny open vendor' archetype specifically. Funded 17 Sep 2025 on Crowd Supply; certified (FCC/CE/UKCA) and first units shipped 4 Feb 2026 - roughly five months from close to first shipment, with follow-up shipping/firmware progress reported 1 Apr 2026. This is the counter-example to 'six-person open startups never deliver': the most open vendor in the category has the cleanest delivery record. Its ceiling is size, not competence - 13.3in maximum.

sources.what_it_supports: Funding, certification and first-shipment dates
Modos's own statement that the Paper Dev Kit shipped to backers, and the Flow spec/openness commitments

historical_precedents.what_happened: MIXED precedent that isolates the real risk. The same campaign that is 10 months late on 28.5in did ship its 7.3in and 13.3in units - promised August 2025, shipping updates posted 1 and 23 December 2025, so about 4 months late, and owners have been using them for ~6 months. The large panel is what slipped by a year. Post-delivery quality is a separate concern: a firmware update (1.8.34) left at least two units showing 'No Battery' and refusing to change images, Wi-Fi transfer failed badly enough that one backer fell back to SD card, and the advertised Home Assistant integration cannot wake the canvas because the Bluetooth wake signal is not exposed.

sources.what_it_supports: Owner reports of 13.3in units in use for months, plus the firmware-bricking, Wi-Fi-transfer and Home-Assistant-wake defects
'SHIPPING' update 1 Dec 2025 and 'Shipping Info' 23 Dec 2025 dating the small/medium fulfilment wave against an Aug 2025 promise

historical_precedents.what_happened: Enumerating Kickstarter's own discovery index for this category (searches run 2026-08-05) turns up only seven successfully funded projects matching 'e ink frame' and 25 matching 'epaper' across the whole history of the platform, of which the >15in ones are exactly three: BLOOMIN8 (28.5in, 10 months late, undelivered), Fraimic (31.5in, 3 months late, DELIVERED), InkJoy (25.3in/28.5in, 3 months late, undelivered). So the crowdfunded >15in population is n=3, and the delivery rate at size is 1 of 3, with the other two still live and communicating rather than dead. Two more >15in campaigns are queued: Memoir (31.5in, Feb 2027 promise) and two unlaunched projects, 'Weclay Paper: Self-Updating Color E-Ink Canvas' and Jitrainno's 'World's First AI-Powered Color E-Ink Art Frame'. Every single one of these campaigns overfunded by 700-11,200%, which is itself a risk factor: none of these teams planned the production volume they now have to deliver.

sources.what_it_supports: The complete set of successfully funded 'e ink frame' projects: BLOOMIN8 (7,991%), Fraimic (11,203%), Memoir (1,789%), PhotoWallet, Moka E-Ink Album, Artink, PixFold
25 successful 'epaper' projects; the only >15in frame among the top 12 is InkJoy; the rest are watches, tablets, dev boards, calendars and signage

Currently live and pre-launch e-ink projects including MelonFrame, 'Weclay Paper: Self-Updating Color E-Ink Canvas', Jitrainno's 'World's First AI-Powered Color E-Ink Art Frame', and BLOOMIN8's second campaign

unverified_facts.claim: The Memento frame used an LCD panel rather than e-paper.
unverified_facts.why_unverified: The page I fetched describes a 35-inch 3:2 4K display but does not name the panel technology; the LCD attribution came from a search-result summary. What IS verified from fetched sources is the size, the ~$900 price, the cloud-only architecture and the bricking. Given a 35in 4K panel in 2016, e-paper is technically implausible, so I am confident it was emissive - but do not cite Memento as an e-paper precedent.
A search summary quoted a Crowd Supply ship date; the Modos Flow page I actually read says only 'Available for pre-order' with no date shown in the extracted text.
